verses.text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to test Jesus. They asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
He answered, “In the evening you say, ‘The weather will be fine—the sky is red.’
“And in the morning you say, ‘Today will be stormy—the sky is red and threatening.’ You know how to read the sky, but you can’t read the signs of the times! Hypocrites!
“An evil and adulterous generation keeps demanding a sign, but no sign will be given except Jonah’s sign.” Then he left them and went away.
When the disciples reached the other side, they realized they’d forgotten to bring bread.
Jesus told them, “Watch out. Be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
They started discussing it among themselves: “He says that because we didn’t bring bread.”
Jesus knew what they were saying. “Why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread, you of little faith?
“Don’t you understand yet? Don’t you remember the five loaves for five thousand people, and how many baskets you collected?
“Or the seven loaves for four thousand people, and how many baskets you collected?
“How did you miss that I wasn’t talking about bread? Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then they understood: he wasn’t warning them about bread yeast, but about the Pharisees’ and Sadducees’ teaching.
When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I, the Son of Man, am?”
They said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some say Elijah, and others say Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But who do you say I am?”
Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered him, “You’re blessed, Simon son of Jonah. No human being revealed this to you; my Father in heaven did.
“I’m telling you: you are Peter, and on this rock I’ll build my church. The gates of Hades won’t overpower it.
“I’ll give you the keys of Heaven’s Kingdom. Whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”
Then he strictly told the disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.
From then on, Jesus began explaining to his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and be raised on the third day.
Peter took him aside and began correcting him: “God forbid, Lord! That will never happen to you!”
Jesus turned to Peter and said, “Get behind me, Satan! You’re a stumbling block to me. You’re thinking about human things, not God’s things.”
Then Jesus told his disciples, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must deny themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it; whoever loses their life for my sake will find it.
“What does someone gain by winning the whole world but losing their life? What could they trade for their life?
“The Son of Man will come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he’ll repay each person according to what they’ve done.
“I’m telling you the truth: some standing here won’t taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
